title: The colors of 1920s posters and advertisements
text: Most area: Light Ivory (5.8%), Tan (3.9%), Olive-Buff (3.2%), Grey Beige (3.1%), Dark Lava (2.2%).

title: The colors of posters and advertisements, 1890-1909
text: Most area: Light Ivory (5.9%), Tan (5.2%), Flesh Red (2.4%), Olive-Buff (2.3%), Stone (2.0%).

title: The colors of wallpaper, 1900-1929
text: Most area: Greyish White (4.5%), Olive-Buff (4.3%), Lion (3.7%), Putty (3.5%), Light Ivory (3.3%).

title: The colors of textiles, 1800-1849
text: Most area: Grey Beige (2.6%), Olive-Buff (2.4%), Linen grey (2.1%), Cool grey (1.8%), Dark Beige (1.8%).

title: The colors of postage stamps, 1930-1969
text: Most area: Platinum (4.8%), Greyish White (2.7%), White (2.0%), Ecru (1.3%), Olive-Buff (1.3%).

title: Colors designers use far more than painters
text: Design (category-balanced) against the 1800-1979 paintings of the corpus, colors in >= 150 design objects: Platinum 8.6x; Light Grey 7.3x; Silver 6.9x; Bluish Grey 6.0x; Cool grey 5.4x; White 5.1x.

title: Colors painters use far more than designers
text: Dark olive brown 12.3x; Ink 5.1x; Bistre 4.6x; Smoky Black 4.5x; Café Noir 3.6x; Brownish Olive 2.9x. (Paintings 1800-1979, n=9797; design n=10577.)

title: Colors that show up in design before painting
text: First decade a color's share passes twice its 1800-1840 level (and holds), design vs painting: Raisin Black 1850s vs 1930s; Platinum 1860s vs 1930s; Linen 1870s vs 1930s; Greenish Black 1860s vs 1910s. Caveat: only public-domain paintings are in the corpus, and few after 1900 (n by decade in the index), so a late painting date is partly a sampling gap.

title: The most vivid, the most muted, the darkest and the lightest decade
text: Mean chroma C* (category-balanced): most vivid 1970s (23.0, n=279), most muted 1860s (12.1, n=553); mean lightness L*: darkest 1930s (52.4), lightest 1940s (64.2). Balanced across 3+ categories per decade.

title: The most saturated and most muted kinds of design
text: Mean chroma C*: Posters and advertisements 20.4 (n=1267) is the most saturated; Glass 10.9 (n=646) the most muted.

title: The most Arts and Crafts color
text: Objects by 5 Arts and Crafts names in our data (n=38: Arthur Heygate Mackmurdo, Christopher Dresser, John Henry Dearle, Walter Crane, William Morris): biggest areas Cool grey, Greenish Black, Silver, Grey Beige; most distinctive vs all design: Brown Red (18.1x), Slate Color (16.5x), Deep maroon (12.4x), Grey (8.7x).

title: The most Art Nouveau color
text: Objects by 13 Art Nouveau names in our data (n=82: Alphonse Mucha, Edward Penfield, Emile Gallé, Eugène Grasset, Georges de Feure, Henri Privat-Livemont...): biggest areas Silver, Black, Tan, Battleship Grey; most distinctive vs all design: Black (6.2x), Yellowish Brown (4.9x), Light Brown (3.9x), Silver (3.9x).

title: The most Bauhaus and modernism color
text: Not enough objects by named Bauhaus and modernism makers in the open data (n=1; the minimum is 15). Most 20th-century modernist work is still in copyright, so its images are not in any open collection.

title: The most Art Deco color
text: Not enough objects by named Art Deco makers in the open data (n=1; the minimum is 15). Most 20th-century modernist work is still in copyright, so its images are not in any open collection.

title: What changed in wallpaper, 1800-1859
text: Colors over-represented in wallpaper of 1800-1859 against all wallpaper in the data: Lavender Grey (1.8x), Papyrus White (1.7x), Ghost White (1.6x).

title: What changed in wallpaper, 1860-1929
text: Colors over-represented in wallpaper of 1860-1929 against all wallpaper in the data: Light Ivory (1.9x), Seafoam Green (1.8x), Lion (1.6x).

title: What changed in textile, 1800-1859
text: Colors over-represented in textile of 1800-1859 against all textile in the data: Benzo Brown (1.7x), Ecru (1.4x), Buffy Brown (1.4x).

title: What changed in textile, 1860-1929
text: Colors over-represented in textile of 1860-1929 against all textile in the data: French Grey (1.3x), White (1.3x).

title: The biggest one-decade color swing
text: Light Ivory went from 0.8% of design area in the 1930s to 6.4% in the 1940s (n=389 and 385, category-balanced).

title: The designer with the most signature color
text: Anonyme, imprimeur (n=12) uses Lion on 55% of the area, 112x the design average.

title: When do vivid modern colors first appear in design?
text: Share of design area in vivid palette colors (C* >= 60), by decade, as category-balanced / commercial only / paintings: 1800s 0.23/0.0/0.47; 1810s 0.24/0.0/0.28; 1820s 0.48/0.0/1.39; 1830s 0.82/0.0/0.34; 1840s 0.62/0.54/0.3; 1850s 0.77/0.12/0.23; 1860s 0.18/0.16/0.05; 1870s 0.33/0.99/0.05; 1880s 0.5/0.46/0.22; 1890s 0.65/0.73/0.22; 1900s 0.61/1.57/0.31; 1910s 0.56/1.37/0.17; 1920s 1.17/2.29/0.37; 1930s 1.32/3.05/1.46; 1940s 2.49/2.73/0.51; 1950s 3.53/4.38/-; 1960s 5.36/6.0/-; 1970s 8.49/8.61/-. Commercial design (advertising, posters, packaging, covers, stamps, products) first passes 6% vivid area in the 1960s. Commercial n=4270; the corpus has no in-copyright 1930-1979 product design, so the late decades rest on posters, stamps and covers.

title: Colors painters (in our corpus) never reach 1% with, that design does
text: 286 named colors never reach 1% of any painting palette in 23306 public-domain paintings (as photographed). 64 of them reach 5% of at least 3 design objects; earliest 10th-percentile year first: Royal plum (1800, n=7); Cream (1801, n=6); Indigo (1806, n=7); Sea Blue (1810, n=4); Yellow Tan (1810, n=6); Merlot (1812, n=6); Russian Violet (1812, n=5); Bishop's Purple (1812, n=8).

title: The colors of commercial design
text: Colors over-represented in commercial design (n=4270) against all other design (n=6307): Greige (2.7x, 0.9% of area), Warm silver (2.7x, 1.3% of area), Biscuit (2.3x, 0.6% of area), Liver Brown (1.9x, 0.7% of area), Bistre (1.8x, 0.7% of area), Mushroom (1.8x, 0.7% of area).

title: The colors of the world's national flags
text: Of 197 national flags (Wikidata and Wikimedia Commons files, colors as drawn there), the most common color words by nearest name: White (132), Smoky Black (43), Lava (41), Gold (34), Lipstick Red (22), Yellow (20), Red (18), Deep royal blue (18).
